title: Cache Method lookups

blocks.text: Looking a member up (`getDeclaredMethod`) is the most expensive part of reflection; invoking a `Method` you already hold is cheap. So frameworks look up once and cache, keyed by `className#methodName(paramTypes)`, and call `setAccessible(true)` once, at lookup, not on every call.
Write `MethodCache`. Its constructor takes a `Finder` (given) that does the real lookup; the tests count its calls.

items: `get(type, name, params...)` returns the method from the cache, or asks the finder **once** and caches it.
The key tells apart **overloads** (the parameter types are part of it) and **classes whose simple names are equal** (it names the class by its full name).
A returned method is **already accessible**: it was made so when it was looked up.
`size()` is the number of cached methods.

cases.says: Two get calls for the same method make one lookup through the finder and return the same Method.
add(int,int) and add(double,double) are two entries and two lookups.
Shop.Item.price and Store.Item.price are two entries, each declared by its own class.
The Method returned for a private method can be invoked at once.

concepts: Member lookup is the most expensive reflective operation, so a Method is looked up once and cached under a key of class, name and parameter types.
